verdict.rationale: Unleash documents its own RBAC at root and project levels, with predefined roles and custom root and project roles for Enterprise users. It also has API tokens scoped to projects and a single environment. However, the documented token scoping covers backend/SDK tokens used for connecting clients, not tokens that restrict who can change flags, and the docs do not detail permission granularity per flag or per environment. RBAC also appears tied to Enterprise/hosted tiers. missing for 10: evidence of granular per-flag or per-environment change permissions, write/admin API tokens scoped to limit flag changes, permission-catalog detail, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can restrict who can change which flags with roles, permissions, and scoped API tokens

citations.quote: Unleash implements role-based access control at root and project levels, with predefined and custom roles for precise permission management.
Enterprise users can create their own custom root roles and custom project roles.
Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
features such as role-based access control, change requests, single sign-on, and SCIM
